n: Vision six: a flying scroll soaring through the air.
The scroll is huge — about 30 by 15 feet (9 by 4.5 meters), the same size as the porch of Solomon’s temple. It is unrolled so all can read it.

f.g: A cubit is about 18 inches (45 cm); so about 30 feet long.

n: The scroll is a curse going out over the land against thieves on one side and those who swear falsely on the other — sins against neighbor and against God.

f.g: Swears falsely — perjury, taking God’s name in vain.

n: God sends the curse into the homes of thieves and perjurers, where it stays and destroys even timber and stone. Sin eats away at a household from within.

f.w: him that sweareth falsely by my name

n: The angel tells Zechariah to look at something else coming out — vision seven.
It is an ephah — a large measuring basket. It represents the sin of people throughout the land.

f.g: A measuring basket holding about 5 gallons (20 liters).
Appearance — or, in some versions, “their iniquity.”

n: A heavy lead lid is lifted, revealing a woman sitting inside the basket.

f.g: A round lead cover weighing about 75 pounds (34 kg).

n: The angel says, “This is Wickedness,” and shoves her back into the basket, slamming the lead lid shut. Evil is contained.
Two women with stork-like wings, carried by the wind, lift the basket into the sky.

f.g: A large migrating bird with a wide wingspan — ironically an unclean bird in the law of Moses.

n: Zechariah asks where they are taking it.

f.w: Whither do these bear the ephah?
f.g: Where is the sin being taken?

n: To Shinar (Babylonia), where a house will be built for it. Wickedness is removed from the holy land and sent back to Babylon — the symbol of worldliness.

f.w: set there upon her own base
f.g: Placed on a pedestal — like an idol in a temple.
